Darda Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Darda, Croatia

Not demolished. Darda's Jewish community formed in 1780 with 34 members but existed only until 1914, when both the community and its synagogue were abandoned; surviving Jews joined the nearby Osijek community. Only 136 Jews lived in Darda before WWII. Darda itself has roots to the 13th century, passing through Ottoman rule (1526-1687, when it was a fortified market town) before joining the Habsburg Monarchy and becoming home to a mixed Hungarian, German, and Croat population known for agricultural production. This cemetery, established in the early 19th century, was abandoned at the end of WWII; its oldest tombstone dates to 1889, its newest to 1940.
